newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MARSEILLE AIM TO START NEW ERA IN WINNING STYLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARSEILLE AIM TO START NEW ERA IN WINNING STYLE.

text.p: Marseille will be looking to cement their new found confidence in the French first division when they play at Cannes on Wednesday and, with one eye on the longer term, ensure they make a winning start to the new post-Tapie era.

The former European champions, currently only under an acting president, recovered from a worrying run of five matches without victory including two successive home defeats by beating Monaco in style at their Velodrome ground last week.
"At Marseille you lose three matches and there's a revolution," the club's incoming president Robert Louis-Dreyfus, chairman of the sportswear giant Adidas, said in an interview published on Tuesday.

Louis-Dreyfus, who succeeded the club's disgraced former president Bernard Tapie at the top at Adidas, told L'Equipe sports daily he would take the reins at Marseille next month, marking the true start of a new era.

The same reasons that made Louis-Dreyfus remark that Marseille can so quickly enter into a major crisis with a few bad results prompted Cannes last week to hold a summit on security arrangements for Wednesday's match.
Fans angered by Marseille's poor run fought with police and also tried to storm the home side's changing rooms after successive home defeats.
Cannes club officials, police and city authorities agreed to consider the match high risk and take appropriate security precautions.
But the much-travelled Louis-Dreyfus said the fervour of Marseille's fans, something he considered had no comparison in England or Germany, had its positive aspects.

"It doesn't always make things easy but... the Marseille crowd is the only one that vibrates in such a manner. This is also an asset," said Louis-Dreyfus, who added he had no reason to think of replacing coach Gerard Gili.
Gili will be looking for the same passion from his players, accused during the poor run of being unworthy of the famous club's colours, as he attempts to string together a run of wins.

Cannes should be easy opposition -- though Marseille will do well to recall they lost at home to lowly Caen and Nantes -- as they have the worst attack in the first division. They have won only once and scored just five goals at home this season.
Yet Marseille captain Jean-Philippe Durand, who is their only doubt with knee trouble, warned: "We mustn't get carried away. The hardest thing is always to confirm (one's form)."

Cannes's beleaguered coach Guy Lacombe said: "We didn't seize our chance in the first half (of the 1-0 defeat) against Bordeaux through lack of drive. We'll need this drive against Marseille to counter their talents."
In view of Cannes' lightweight attack, Gili is expected again to field a three-man defence with Italian central defender Alberto Malusci, back from suspension, starting on the bench.
